from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        lecture_lines = [
            "Fourier coefficients act as volume knobs for harmonics.",

        ]

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Fourier series can be viewed as rotating gears.",
            "Phasors spin at speeds determined by their frequency.",
            "The path of the final gear traces complex shapes.",
            "Epicycles draw any silhouette with pure harmonic rotations.",
            "Geometry visualizes the math of oscillating signals."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Series", lecture_lines)
        
        # Load Assets
        gear_asset = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/gear.svg")
        
        # Define objects
        wave = SineWave(amplitude=1, frequency=1)
        # Fixes from VideoCritic (Line 59 adjustment / grid usage)
        self.place_in_area(wave, 'D2', 'F5', scale_factor=0.6)
        wave_dot = Dot(color="#FF0000")
        self.place_at_grid(wave_dot, 'E3', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        gears = VGroup(*[gear_asset.copy().set_color("#FFFFFF") for _ in range(3)])
        gears.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(gears, 'B2', 'C5', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(gears))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.add(wave, wave_dot)
        self.play(Create(wave), MoveAlongPath(wave_dot, wave), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        gear_final = gear_asset.copy().set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(gear_final, 'F4', scale_factor=0.4)
        self.play(FadeIn(gear_final))
        self.wait(1)

class SineWave(VMobject):
    def __init__(self, amplitude=1, frequency=1, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        self.set_points_smoothly([
            np.array([x, amplitude * np.sin(frequency * x), 0])
            for x in np.linspace(-2, 2, 100)
        ])
        self.set_color("#FFFF00")

outline.topic: Pure Fourier Series: Decoding Signals into Simple Harmonics

sections.title: Prerequisites & Intuition (0:00-0:45)
sections.content: Briefly review the concept of periodic functions and the idea of 'basis vectors'. Use an analogy: Just as a coordinate system (x, y, z) defines any point in 3D space, a set of sine/cosine waves can 'build' any periodic signal.
sections.example: A musical chord: Explain how our ears perceive one complex sound, while the Fourier series shows it is just a stack of individual pure piano keys pressed together.

sections.title: The Fundamental Hypothesis (0:45-1:45)
sections.content: Introduce the Fourier Series formula. Explain that any periodic function f(x) can be expressed as an infinite sum of sines and cosines. Visualize this as 'layering' waves of increasing frequencies (harmonics).
sections.example: Use a visual animation showing a 'Square Wave' being constructed. Start with one sine wave (fundamental frequency), then add a third harmonic, then a fifth, showing how the edges become sharper and 'squarer' with each addition.

sections.title: Calculating Coefficients (1:45-3:15)
sections.content: Explain the role of the Fourier Coefficients (a_n, b_n). These are the 'weights' or 'volume knobs' for each harmonic. Introduce the orthogonality property of trigonometric functions visually—how integration filters out all components except the one being isolated.
sections.example: The 'Sound Mixing Board': Imagine a mixing board where a_n and b_n are sliders. Adjusting a slider changes the contribution of that specific harmonic to the final 'sound' or wave shape.

sections.title: Visualizing the Series (3:15-4:15)
sections.content: Present the geometric interpretation. Show a rotating vector (phasor) representation. Explain that the Fourier series is essentially rotating 'gears' of different sizes and speeds, where the tip of the final gear traces the target signal.
sections.example: The 'Epic Cycle' animation: Show how epicycles (circles tracing circles) can draw a complex periodic shape, like a cartoon character's silhouette, using only pure harmonic rotations.

sections.title: Application & Summary (4:15-5:00)
sections.content: Conclude with real-world utility: Image compression (JPEG), noise cancellation in headphones, and signal processing. Emphasize that the Fourier Series turns a complex time-domain mess into a simple, ordered frequency-domain list.
sections.example: Noise-Canceling Headphones: The device captures a chaotic street noise, calculates its Fourier components, and generates an 'anti-noise' wave to perfectly cancel out those specific harmonics.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: Objects are placed too close to the center, causing potential visual clutter with the left-aligned lecture text. Fix: Line 65: self.place_at_grid(group_a, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8); Line 68: self.place_at_grid(group_b, 'B5', scale_factor=0.8) (line=65, object=group_a and group_b)
issues.resolution_note: Applied suggested grid placements and scaling.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: Inadequate use of the right-side grid leads to a cramped layout; elements should be distributed vertically to provide more breathing room. Fix: Line 65: self.place_at_grid(group_a, 'B3', scale_factor=0.9); Line 68: self.place_at_grid(group_b, 'E3', scale_factor=0.9) (line=68, object=group_a and group_b)
issues.resolution_note: Distributed elements vertically (B2, B5, E3) to improve layout.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: Labels (A and B) are inconsistent in scale and risk being obscured by the grid labels. issues.resolution_note: Standardized label scale and improved positioning to avoid occlusion.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The formula at B2 creates visual crowding and lacks sufficient breathing room from the lecture notes on the left. Fix: Line 68: self.place_at_grid(formula, 'C3', scale_factor=0.9) (line=68, object=formula)
